scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 7 · Temperature and its Measurement
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, medical diagnosis, treatment recommendation, thermometer safety certification or permission for hazardous temperature experiments.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 7 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion while preserving no-touch-testing, no-mercury/broken-glass, no-boiling/flame and no-medical-diagnosis boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner treats a hot/cold sensation as an exact temperature measurement, for example claiming that an object that feels cold must be below 0 °C.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use teacher-provided sensation-versus-measurement cards to label each statement as sensation, thermometer measurement or interpretation, then revise claims so only the instrument-supported temperature is reported numerically.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly separates sensation from measured temperature in unfamiliar examples and rejects unsupported numerical conclusions based on touch alone.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that two materials which feel different to the hand must have different temperatures and does not distinguish measurement from interpretation.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied classroom cards describing materials at the same stated thermometer reading but different touch sensations, and explain why the sensation does not replace the measured evidence; do not touch unknown hot or cold materials.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses thermometer evidence rather than sensation to compare unfamiliar cases and clearly distinguishes observation, measurement and interpretation.

scenarios.need: Learner confuses thermometer range with least count, counts printed marks instead of intervals or omits the Celsius unit.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use supplied thermometer diagrams to identify labelled endpoints, count equal intervals, calculate the value per interval, state the full range separately and record readings with °C.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly determines range and least count from unfamiliar scale diagrams, reads the indicated value and includes °C without confusing marks and intervals.

scenarios.need: Learner reports many unsupported decimal places because more digits are assumed to mean a more accurate temperature.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied scale diagrams and digital-display examples, identify the displayed or marked resolution and rewrite each reading using only precision supported by the instrument evidence.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Rejects false precision in unfamiliar examples and reports temperature values with a defensible number of digits and the correct unit.

scenarios.need: Learner chooses an unsuitable thermometer for a task or ignores the instrument range and placement instructions.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Match teacher-provided task cards to intact adult-approved digital or laboratory-style thermometer cards by stated range and purpose, then identify the required safe placement and stable-reading condition without performing hazardous heating.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Selects a suitable instrument for unfamiliar safe scenarios, checks range and method, and explains why an unsuitable instrument should not be used.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes touching an unknown hot liquid, using a mercury or broken-glass thermometer, boiling water, using flame, handling a hot vessel or using mains-powered heating to create a larger temperature change.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the hazardous plan and replace it with supplied temperature data, safe moderate-temperature samples or an intact adult-approved digital probe; never touch-test unknown hot material or use mercury, broken glass, boiling water, flame, hot vessels or mains heating.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Consistently identifies each hazardous temperature-measurement proposal, states the relevant hazard and substitutes a safe evidence-based classroom method.

scenarios.need: Learner treats one body-temperature reading as a complete diagnosis or proposes treatment based on the classroom exercise.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a supplied hypothetical body-temperature statement to separate the numerical measurement from medical interpretation, state that the learning activity does not diagnose or prescribe, and escalate genuine health concerns to a trusted adult and appropriate healthcare guidance without collecting learner medical data.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly limits a body-temperature example to measurement evidence, rejects diagnosis or treatment claims from one reading and identifies appropriate adult/healthcare escalation.

scenarios.need: Learner needs concise offline temperature practice without uploading a photo, body-temperature reading, medical history or personal information.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached thermometer diagrams, synthetic temperature tables and instrument-choice cards locally to calculate least count, read °C values and compare trends without photo upload, body-temperature collection, medical-history collection, microphone, camera, precise location, telemetry or network-dependent tutoring.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline synthetic task using supplied evidence only, reads and compares temperatures correctly, and discloses no personal, medical or sensor-derived learner data.
